extracted.intended_audience: pharmaceutical companies, biosimilars applicants, reference product sponsors, and patent litigators advising on BPCIA compliance
extracted.subtask_description: A step-by-step guide to the obligations, timing, and remedies under 42 U.S.C. § 262(l) (the BPCIA 'patent dance') for biosimilar applicants and reference product sponsors, including case-law clarifications and contested issues. Useful for counseling on compliance, litigation timing, and strategic choices under the statute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant provides aBLA and manufacturing information (l)(2)(A)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant provides a copy of its aBLA and manufacturing information to the Reference Product Sponsor (RPS). (42 U.S.C. § 262(l)(2)(A))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timing: within 20 days of FDA acceptance (timeline shows 'Within 20 Days'). Consequences: availability of certain declaratory-judgment actions and interplay with other l provisions depend on whether this disclosure is made; case law has disputed effects of providing/withholding (see l(9) discussion).

rubrics_metrics.name: RPS provides list of potentially infringed patents (l)(3)(A)(i)
rubrics_metrics.description: RPS must provide the Applicant with a list of patents that could potentially be infringed by the Applicant's product. (42 U.S.C. § 262(l)(3)(A)(i))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timing: within 60 days after receipt of the aBLA and manufacturing information (timeline shows 'Within 60 Days'). This list starts the process for First Wave litigation and subsequent negotiations.

rubrics_metrics.name: RPS identifies patents it is willing to license (l)(3)(A)(ii)
rubrics_metrics.description: From its list, RPS must identify any patents that it is willing to license to the Applicant. (42 U.S.C. § 262(l)(3)(A)(ii))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included with the RPS's (l)(3)(A) list; pertinent to settlement/licensing negotiations and potential narrowing of disputes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant may provide list of patents Applicant believes could reasonably be asserted (l)(3)(B)(i)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant may give the RPS a list of patents that the Applicant believes could reasonably be asserted against it. (42 U.S.C. § 262(l)(3)(B)(i))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This list is used in the parties' exchange/negotiation process to determine which patents proceed to litigation and influences limits on the RPS's subsequent list size.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant must respond to each RPS patent with detailed statement or covenant (l)(3)(B)(ii)(I)-(II)
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 60 days, the Applicant must respond to each patent on the RPS's (l)(3)(A) list with either: (i) a detailed statement of invalidity, unenforceability, or noninfringement, OR (ii) a statement that the Applicant will not commercially market the product before patent expiration. (42 U.S.C. § 262(l)(3)(B)(ii)(I)-(II))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timing: within 60 days. Practical note: whether an Applicant may 'waive' the right to receive this detailed statement (to speed the dance) has been disputed in litigation (e.g., Amgen v. Sandoz).

rubrics_metrics.name: RPS must provide detailed statement of validity, enforceability, and infringement (l)(3)(C)
rubrics_metrics.description: If Applicant provides a detailed statement under l(3)(B), the RPS must provide Applicant with a detailed statement of validity, enforceability, and infringement for each patent addressed. (42 U.S.C. § 262(l)(3)(C))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timing: within 60 days (timeline indicates RPS provides this within 60 days after Applicant's (l)(3)(B) statement). This exchanges technical and legal positions pre-litigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parties negotiate which patents to litigate (l)(4) and simultaneous exchange/lists (l)(5)(B)(i)
rubrics_metrics.description: After the statements are exchanged, the parties negotiate which patents will be litigated and simultaneously exchange lists of patents to be litigated. (42 U.S.C. §§ 262(l)(4), (l)(5)(B)(i))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timing: negotiations begin immediately after the (l)(3)(C) statement; specific short deadlines appear in the statute/timeline (e.g., within 15 days for some steps). Whether an Applicant may decline to participate in the negotiation process has been disputed but not resolved in case law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit on number of patents RPS may list (l)(5)(B)(ii)
rubrics_metrics.description: The number of patents on RPS's list cannot exceed the number of patents on Applicant's list; if the Applicant's list has zero patents, RPS may list one patent. (42 U.S.C. § 262(l)(5)(B)(ii))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This statutory numeric limit governs the scope of First Wave litigation and is a key strategic constraint for RPS. Timing: applies during the simultaneous-list exchange under l(5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant identifies number of patents Applicant believes should be litigated (l)(5)(A)
rubrics_metrics.description: If parties do not agree which patents to litigate, Applicant must identify the number of patents it believes should be litigated. (42 U.S.C. § 262(l)(5)(A))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This identification feeds into the process used to select patents for First Wave litigation when negotiations fail.

rubrics_metrics.name: RPS files First Wave litigation within 30 days of l(5) disclosure (l)(6)(A)-(B)
rubrics_metrics.description: The RPS shall file First Wave litigation within 30 days of the information disclosure set forth in § 262(l)(5). (42 U.S.C. § 262(l)(6)(A)-(B))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the RPS fails to file within 30 days, its only remedy in a later infringement action on the First Wave patents may be damages equal to a reasonable royalty (35 U.S.C. § 271(e)(6)(B)). Case law (e.g., Janssen v. Celltrion) has held parties must engage in good-faith negotiations and the specified dispute-resolution procedure to preserve certain remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant notifies FDA that suit has been filed (l)(6)(C)
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 30 days after RPS files First Wave litigation, the Applicant must notify the FDA that suit has been filed. (42 U.S.C. § 262(l)(6)(C))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This notice interfaces with FDA's approval/launch timeline and the Applicant's later commercial-marketing notice obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: RPS must supplement list for newly issued/licensed patents (l)(7)
rubrics_metrics.description: RPS must supplement its patent list with relevant newly issued or licensed patents within 30 days of issuance or licensing; any such patents listed will be subject to the Second Wave of patent litigation. (42 U.S.C. § 262(l)(7))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timing: 30 days after issuance/licensing. Newly listed patents are treated as candidates for the second wave; strategic monitoring of patent issuances/licenses is essential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant must provide notice of commercial marketing (l)(8)(A))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Applicant must notify the RPS that it intends to commercially market the product at least 180 days before launch. (42 U.S.C. § 262(l)(8)(A))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Federal Circuit (Amgen v. Apotex) held that an Applicant must provide the l(8)(A) commercial-marketing notice regardless of whether the Applicant provided (l)(2)(A) disclosures. The Supreme Court (Sandoz v. Amgen) ruled the Applicant may provide the notice either before or after receiving FDA approval. Practical deadline in statute: at least 180 days before launch.

rubrics_metrics.name: RPS may seek preliminary injunction after Applicant's commercial-marketing notice (l)(8)(B))
rubrics_metrics.description: Immediately after the Applicant provides the commercial-marketing notice, the RPS may seek a preliminary injunction prohibiting commercial launch until the court rules on any patents listed by RPS or Applicant in l(3) or l(7) that were not subject to First Wave litigation. (42 U.S.C. § 262(l)(8)(B))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides a statutory basis for immediate pre-launch injunctive relief on non-First-Wave patents; timing is 'Immediately after notification' per the timeline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on declaratory-judgment actions when Applicant provides l(2)(A) (l)(9)(A))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Applicant provides the (l)(2)(A) application and information, neither RPS nor Applicant may file a declaratory-judgment (DJ) action for First Wave Litigation patents. (42 U.S.C. § 262(l)(9)(A))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This restricts preemptive DJ filings for patents designated for First Wave litigation when the statutory exchange has occurred.

rubrics_metrics.name: RPS may file DJ action if Applicant provides l(2)(A) but fails other steps (l)(9)(B))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Applicant provides (l)(2)(A) information but fails to complete one of the remaining steps in (l)(3)-(8), the RPS may file a DJ action for any (l)(3)(A) or (l)(7) patent. (42 U.S.C. § 262(l)(9)(B))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarification from Amgen v. Apotex: (l)(9)(B) does not make declaratory judgments exclusive and does not eliminate remedies provided in 35 U.S.C. § 271(e)(4). Case law may affect strategy and remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: RPS may file DJ action if Applicant does not provide l(2)(A) (l)(9)(C))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Applicant does not provide the (l)(2)(A) application and information, the RPS may file a DJ action for any patent that claims Applicant's product or its use. (42 U.S.C. § 262(l)(9)(C))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to make the initial statutory disclosure opens broader options for RPS to seek declaratory relief on patents claiming the product or its use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory and case-law disputes/uncertainties (waiver, negotiation participation, filing obligations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Several practical and interpretive issues arising under the BPCIA remain disputed in litigation, including whether an Applicant may 'waive' the right to receive the detailed (l)(3)(B)(ii) statement, whether an Applicant may decline to participate in the l(4)/l(5) negotiation process, and whether an RPS must file suit within 30 days if the Applicant 'waived' subsequent patent-dance steps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are unresolved questions highlighted by ongoing case law (e.g., Amgen v. Sandoz; Immunex v. Sandoz; Amgen v. Hospira; Janssen v. Celltrion). Counsel should monitor developments and consider strategic implications of waiver or nonparticipation.
